stages.prompt:
Use case: style-transfer.
Asset type: a comparison example for the original 2D pixel game Mosslight, not a new approved art direction.
Input image 1: EDIT TARGET. Preserve this image's scene design, location, object placement, architecture, character outfit and identity.
Input image 2: STYLE REFERENCE A ONLY. Transfer its precise visual rendering language across the entire target image. Do not copy its building design, map layout, character costume, bridges, boat, or extra props.
Primary request: redraw image 1 as though the same pixel artist who painted image 2 had rendered it. The change in craftsmanship and mood must be clearly visible, not merely a color filter or superficial sharpening.
Transfer A's traits: fine, deliberate square pixel clusters and stepped edges; intricate handmade storybook textures; detailed moss, fine ferns and individually articulated tiny leaves; subtle irregular wood grain and aged stone; restrained sparse dithering; finely observed fabric folds; delicate flowers; gentle nuanced material-specific shading; deep navy forest shadows and small pools of warm honey light. More intimate and quietly mysterious than the bright toy-like target, yet still cute and welcoming. Use A's smaller, more disciplined detail clusters and naturalistic surface treatment rather than large puffy uniform highlight patches. Preserve pixel art, no smooth paint or 3D. Use colored selective outlines like A, avoid heavy cartoon outlines. Readable silhouettes must survive this finer detail.
Layout invariant: same landscape 16:9 crop and overhead three-quarter camera as image 1, same cottage upper left, same pond and waterfall upper right, same winding stone path and planting beds, same protagonist location, same plants and lamp designs. No zoom, no added floor, no changed facade layout, no replacement building, no added object or character. Preserve the original rounded/curling shapes where they exist; reinterpret surfaces and lighting, not the architecture or costumes.
Keep existing clothing silhouette and base proportions, small cute eyes and cheeks. The character must stay recognizable as the person in image 1. Keep the original palette families of this scene while adopting A's more restrained chroma, shadow depth and nuanced warm/cool balance. Do not turn both variants into the same green forest.
No text, labels, HUD, logos, watermarks, borders, inset panels or comparison montage. One finished full-frame image.
TARGET B SPECIFICS: Retain the original squat round cottage with low broad GREEN moss roof, left chimney, left round cross-mullioned glowing window and right arched wooden door. Retain the green/teal woodland, round tree masses, creamy walls, little white flowers, original pond dock, stump and small white woodland creature. Protagonist keeps the original ROUND SAGE-GREEN hood, peach neckerchief, sage outfit, cream tunic, short boots, little brown satchel, and small warm brass hand lantern, in the exact original pose. Do not give them C's pointed purple hood. Preserve the round moss-capped stone garden lamp, blue pompon crops and hanging golden bell crops. Keep B's round playful design, but render all of it with A's finer crafted moss/wood/fabric textures and quieter night lighting.

Very important: hat points, pompom, or folded tips are accessories above the actual head and do NOT count toward the anatomical head-to-body ratio.
Preserve all scene pixels as closely as possible: cottage design, roof, doors, crops, lamp, pond, paths, plants and lighting. The correction is confined to the protagonist's silhouette and necessary adjacent ground. Retain the already-achieved fine, textured A-style pixel craftsmanship.
No labels, text, HUD, logos, watermark or panels.
B costume invariants: ROUND sage-green hood, peach neckerchief, sage cloak over cream tunic, brown satchel and boots, honey-gold handheld lantern.
